findings.title: Global sign-out ran after the throwing audit bookkeeping
findings.question: error-handling
findings.whatBreaks: completePasswordReset called onReset() (clear_sign_in_failures + log_event, which throw on a DB error) BEFORE signOutEverywhere(). If onReset threw, the password was already changed but the global sign-out was skipped and the route (no try/catch) returned a raw 500 - leaving pre-existing sessions alive after a recovery, the exact thing 'end all sessions' defends against.
findings.evidence: passwordReset.ts (pre-fix): onReset() awaited, then signOutEverywhere(); reset-password/route.ts has no try/catch. The edge change+event-atomic rule does not bind this Next route (ADR-0005).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED in a7ea266. signOutEverywhere() now runs BEFORE onReset(), and onReset is best-effort: it reports a DB failure via report() instead of throwing, so a bookkeeping hiccup cannot drop the (already-applied) session revocation. Unit test asserts sign-out precedes the bookkeeping.

findings.title: Fail-open collapses tampered/deleted cookie with absent cookie; the idle/absolute timeout is bypassable at an authenticated workstation, and the ADR overstated the guarantee
findings.question: error-handling
findings.evidence: readActivity returns null on HMAC failure (sessionActivity.ts:93) and on absence; middleware maps any null to allow (middleware.ts:48,56; sessionGate.ts:36). getUser() refreshes the Supabase session each pass, so the activity cookie is the ONLY idle/absolute enforcement; RLS enforces aal2, not session age. An attacker at an unattended workstation can delete tp-activity and the timeout never fires. RESOLVED (not a blind code change — the fail-open is a sound availability choice): (1) ADR-0010 Consequences corrected to state the timeout is best-effort/bypassable by cookie deletion and that RLS does not backstop session age (the prior 'treated by its true age' claim was inaccurate); (2) added a @security fail-open scenario (safe-sessions.feature 'A deleted activity cookie fails open...') so the posture is tested and owned; (3) added a TODO for the fail-closed-after-grace hardening (stamp at sign-in; needs the deferred session registry).

findings.title: Activity route called internalCallSecret() outside any try/catch — a missing INTERNAL_CALL_SECRET threw an unhandled 500 instead of the documented graceful degradation
